column1: # roborepo install manifest — single source of truth for managed home<->repo paths.
# Hand-duplicated across 7+ scripts before this file existed (install/main.sh,
#   harness   claude | codex | gemini        which harness this row belongs to
#   kind      link | root_config | cleanup    behavior (see below)
#   src_rel   path under repo root, or "-" for cleanup rows (no repo source)
#   home_sub  path relative to the harness home dir (claude=~/.claude, codex=~/.codex,
#             gemini=~/.gemini); the reader joins the home root
#   home_root home dir token: claude=~/.claude  codex=~/.codex  gemini=~/.gemini
#               nodoctor  = not checked by doctor --installed (verify still checks)
#               nosync    = not pulled from live home config by the installer / update path
#   managed_copy   roborepo-owned copy: repo src copied to home_sub on install/update,
#                  reclaimed on uninstall if content still matches repo source.
#   root_config    mutable user state: copied not linked, adopt-on-collision
#   rendered_rules generated file: written by rules-render.mjs from base fragments +
#                  enabled-packages registry; src_rel is "-" (no single source file);
#                  user's original is backed up to pre-install dir before first render.
#   hook_fragment  a hooks file packages also merge into: the source's `hooks` map merges
#                  through the provider's hooks.merge and unmerges on removal, entry by entry.
#   managed_files  a directory packages also copy into: each source file is copied and
#                  tracked by hash; only unedited copies are updated or removed.
# commands/ is no longer a manifest row: it is composed at install/update time from only the
# install-lib.sh), not copied as one static repo-wide directory. See Phase 7 of the ownership plan.
# git-hooks/ installs with the base root config, whose env points agent git at it: if the config
# shipped without these files, agent shells would run no git hooks at all, the repo's own included.
# It is a sibling of hooks/, not inside it, because a managed_files row owns everything under its target.
